Computing

Systems and Searching

Six lessons. It begins with what a system is: parts that work together. That idea runs right through to how a search engine finds, ranks and shapes the results a person sees. Builds on Year 3 Connecting Computers and Year 4 The Internet.

Words for this unit

More are added as each lesson is built.

What do we call two or more devices joined together?

a network

Name a device that can connect to a network.

laptop, tablet, phone, printer, games console

What is the job of a server?

it stores information and shares it with other devices

What do you think the word system means?

By the end of today

  • Explain that a system is built from a number of parts
  • Describe the input, process and output of a digital system
  • Show how the parts of a system communicate with each other

Can you name the parts of this bicycle?

Some parts work together for one job

PartHandlebars
PartFront fork
JobThe bike steers

Turn the handlebars, the fork turns, the front wheel points a new way. That's the steering system.

Find another system on the bike

Use the activity sheet. Pick the pedals and chain, the brakes, or a wheel. Draw the parts and write how they work together.

Explain to the person next to you: what is a system?

A system is a set of parts that work together to do a task. The parts might be components, devices, or people.

Systems and Searching · Lesson 1

Systems

Your task

Design a system of your own: a smart bin, a smart nightlight, a smart pencil case, or your own idea. Draw it, then write:

  • its input: what happens to start it working (not just a body part — say what the system detects or receives)
  • its process: what the system works out or decides
  • its output: what it does as a result

Last, think of one more thing it could do.
